newsitem.title: USA: FBI interviews airline crew about flare-like object.
newsitem.headline: FBI interviews airline crew about flare-like object.

text.p: The FBI is interviewing a Saudi Arabian Airlines crew about a flare-like object they saw in the sky in New York near Kennedy International Airport, federal law enforcement officials said Thursday.
They said FBI agents had been sent to question the crew at Dulles Airport in a nearby Virginia suburb, where the plane landed, in an attempt to determine precisely what they saw.

The FBI was interested because of the crash in July of TWA Flight 800, which exploded and fell into the Atlantic Ocean just minutes after taking off from Kennedy airport. The FBI is trying to determine if a bomb, missile or mechanical failure caused the jet to crash.
The officials were at a loss to explain what the Saudi crew had observed earlier Thursday. "It could be anything," one official said.
They also were unsure what significance, if any, it would have for the TWA investigation, which has enountered problems in pinpointing the cause of the crash.
"It may turn out to be completely nothing. I can't say there is anything to it. Obviously, if someone reports something, they have to check it out. That's standard," one official said.
A Federal Aviation Administration official said the crew of the 747, flying at about 12,000 feet, spotted the green flare while making the approach to Kennedy.
But, the official said, the pilot did not feel the plane was in jeopardy and simply reported it as a "sighting."
